column1: # Branches that state an outcome after testing a request field, and are
# §11's rule is: never assert an outcome the response did not carry.
# `gates outcomes` holds the checkable shape of it — a branch that tests
# a boolean the caller sent, and then writes the sentence describing the
# result, without asking Drive anything. That is how `lock_file` came to
# report a lock Drive had not applied, printed directly above a card
# Two shapes are excluded by the rule itself rather than by this file: a
# dry run, which makes no call by construction and says "would" (the
# honest form of exactly this sentence), and a refusal, which says what
# THIS SERVER did and is true whatever Drive would have answered.
# Columns, tab-separated: file:Field, and the reason. A row that stops
# matching a branch fails, so an excuse cannot outlive the code it

column2: the count comes from the listing Drive just answered, and what the sentence claims — that this server left those drives out — is this server's own filtering, which is the one thing it can assert without asking anybody

it states what Drive was ASKED to do and says outright that Drive does not report whether it did, then names list_comments as the call that settles it. The sentence this replaced said the threads "were copied with it", which files.copy cannot know — it answers with a File and mentions comments nowhere. Reading it back was the other option and was rejected: comments.list lags a copy, so an empty answer would report threads as dropped when they were merely late
